title: Ratchet a tie-down strap taut over a crate to the deck's D-rings and latch its handle before the deck is jolted
instruction: Strap the crate down to the deck.
context: Drivers and loaders tie each item down before a vehicle moves. Cargo-securement rules (49 CFR 393.100-136, EN 12195-1) and ratchet makers' instructions agree: run the strap over the load to anchor points on the deck, take it up with full strokes of the ratchet handle until it is tight, then close the handle flat until it locks. A slack strap does not press the load onto the deck, so it slides or tips when the vehicle brakes. Here a tall crate stands on a deck section with a slack strap over its top from one floor D-ring to a ratchet hooked in another; after the robot lets go, the deck runs into a hard stop. Tension builds over lever strokes held by a pawl, the lever is latched, and a braking jolt tests it. O*NET task for heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers (53-3032.00, about 2.1M US jobs, BLS OEWS 2025): 'Secure cargo for transport, using ropes, blocks, chain, binders, or covers.' Also done by light truck drivers and freight and material movers (53-3033.00, 53-7062.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), everything square to the table; heights above the deck's top. Deck section: a steel chequer plate 24 x 32 x 1 cm centred at x 29, y -11, its top 1.2 cm above the table, ballasted underneath so it and its carriage move 20 kg in all, on a linear slide along x: 15 cm of travel from a rear stop (the start) to a steel end stop in front. Bolted to it: two zinc floor D-rings, their bars 4.4 cm long along x and 0.8 cm up, at x 28.3, y +2.5 and y -24.5. A pine crate ballasted to 1 kg, 5.5 cm front to back, 10 cm wide, 14 cm tall, stands centred at x 28.3, y -11 on painted corner marks. The tie-down is yellow polyester webbing 3 cm wide, 100 g, its centre line at x 28.3. Its fixed end is looped through the left D-ring (via an inline load cell on the real rig); taut, it runs straight up 15.7 cm to the crate's top left edge (58 deg to the deck), 10.3 cm across the top, and 7.2 cm down toward the right D-ring into the mandrel of a steel lever ratchet for 3 cm webbing, whose hook is in the right D-ring and whose frame lies along that leg (the leg is 15.7 cm, ring to edge). The mandrel's axis runs along x, 8.5 cm up the leg from the ring (y -20.0, 7.9 cm up). Taut, the strap is 33.3 cm from ring to mandrel; at the start 12 mm more is paid out, so it stands up to 12 mm off the crate's top. The handle: two steel side plates 5 cm apart pivoting on the mandrel's axis, 60 g in all, joined by a round red PVC-sleeved grip bar 1 cm thick and 4.6 cm long along x, 6.4 cm back down the leg from the axis and 2.5 cm out from it when shut. Shut (0 deg) it lies back down the leg; it opens up and away from the crate; it starts 40 deg open.
scoring: From the poses of the deck, crate, strap and handle (on a real rig: the strap's tension on the load cell at its fixed end, the handle's angle on a protractor plate round its axis, and the crate's position on the deck from video against marks). Taut = 50 N or more in the strap. In sim the tension is the take-up spring's force: each full stroke (handle out past 75 deg, then back under 35 deg) winds 5 mm, and the strap end is held short of the wound length only by the strap pressing on the crate, at 8 N per mm (4 strokes give about 60 N, 3 about 20 N); on a real rig the load cell reads it (calibration in the README). Latched: pressed to within 1 deg of shut, and within 1.5 deg now. The jolt: once both grippers have been 3 cm clear of the crate, strap and handle and everything still for 1 s, the deck runs 15 cm into its stop at about 0.38 m/s; it is over 1 s after the stop. Held down: through the jolt the crate's bottom and top centres move no more than 2.5 mm and it tips no more than 2 deg on the deck. Fail, latched for the trial (score 0): the handle opened to 130 deg (strap let out), the crate moved over 3 mm or 2 deg before the jolt, or not held down. Score: 0.25 for taut; with that, +0.25 for latched; with both, +0.5 once the jolt is over. Halved unless both grippers are 2.5 cm clear of the crate, strap and handle and they are still. 1.0 is success, held for 1 s. Scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Engage the deck's catch first. Pull the ratchet's release, open the handle and pay the strap out to its slack mark (12 mm past taut in sim; on a real rig the mark set at calibration so 3 full strokes read under 50 N and 4 read 50 N or more), set the handle 40 deg open, stand the crate on its marks under the strap, and run the deck back by hand onto its rear stop (raising the drive weight) until the catch holds it. Real rig: the deck is pulled by a 1.0 kg weight on a cord over a pulley (10 N, so at most about 0.4 m/s at the stop), held by a catch that fails safe (stays engaged without power), inside a fixed guard with an e-stop; the load cell is zeroed with the strap slack. Calibration, the stop and the guarding are in the README.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid boxes, one shared friction (1.2/1.0). The strap is four rigid webbing links hinged across their width: it bends over the crate's edges but cannot stretch, twist or swing out of its plane. Its tension is a take-up spring (8 kN/m, the webbing's stretch) from the strap end to the wound length, set 5 mm per full stroke by a per-step pawl rule. The handle is a friction hinge with a detent and latch rule; its winding torque and the ratchet swinging on its hook are not modelled.
